finding.title: boundary/length_plus_one: unhandled server error
finding.description: 1 case(s) in boundary/length_plus_one produced unhandled server error -- the endpoint returned an unhandled 5xx; where health still answered afterwards the request failed but the service survived, which is not unavailability. Severity is scored from the single highest-scoring instance; the 1 affected case(s) indicate reproducibility, not impact.
finding.remediation: 1 case(s) observed as 500x1. Check the tokenized length against the model's maximum sequence length before inference and reject over-limit input with a typed 4xx response. Do not add truncation: silently shortening the input would hide the failure this case exists to measure.

remediation_detail.observed: 1 of 1 cited case row(s) were available; recorded outcomes: HTTP 500: 1; post-request health-check failures: 0.
remediation_detail.significance: Input at or beyond the model's sequence limit produced a server-error response rather than a defined rejection. The settled architecture forbids silent truncation, so rejecting is the intended behaviour and erroring is not.
remediation_detail.fix: Check the tokenized length against the model's maximum sequence length before inference and reject over-limit input with a typed 4xx response. Do not add truncation: silently shortening the input would hide the failure this case exists to measure.

verification.expected: over-limit cases return the documented 4xx rejection and under-limit cases still return 200
verification.inspect: results/verify_sentiment_v1/results_sentiment_v1.jsonl -- check the rows whose attack_id is one of: boundary.length.plus_one

finding.remediation: 1 case(s) observed as 200x1. Tighten request-model validation so this shape is rejected with a 422: strict field types and forbidding unexpected fields, checked before any inference call.

remediation_detail.observed: 1 of 1 cited case row(s) were available; recorded outcomes: HTTP 200: 1; post-request health-check failures: 0.
remediation_detail.significance: The pre-registered oracle for this case says the request should have been rejected, but the endpoint accepted it and answered. A confident answer to a structurally invalid request is a schema-enforcement gap, not a model problem.
remediation_detail.fix: Tighten request-model validation so this shape is rejected with a 422: strict field types and forbidding unexpected fields, checked before any inference call.

finding.title: malformed/oversized_10mb: hit the request timeout
finding.description: 1 case(s) in malformed/oversized_10mb produced hit the request timeout -- no response was produced within the 10 second deadline; the recorded error is client-side and carries no server-stage information, so no cause is attributed. Severity is scored from the single highest-scoring instance; the 1 affected case(s) indicate reproducibility, not impact.
finding.remediation: 1 case(s) observed as no responsex1. Bound the work a single request can do before the deadline: reject oversized bodies at the server layer and cap per-request inference time. Establishing the cause needs server-side timing instrumentation this run did not collect.

remediation_detail.observed: 1 of 1 cited case row(s) were available; recorded outcomes: no response: 1; post-request health-check failures: 0.
remediation_detail.significance: No response was produced inside the request deadline. The recorded error is client-side and carries no server-stage information, so where the time went is not established by this evidence.
remediation_detail.fix: Bound the work a single request can do before the deadline: reject oversized bodies at the server layer and cap per-request inference time. Establishing the cause needs server-side timing instrumentation this run did not collect.

verification.expected: the same case returns a bounded response or a documented rejection inside the deadline
verification.inspect: results/verify_sentiment_v1/results_sentiment_v1.jsonl -- check the rows whose attack_id is one of: malformed.oversized_10mb

remediation_detail.significance: The top label changed under a transformation intended to preserve meaning, while the clean prediction was confident. This is a model-level sensitivity: the input reached the model unchanged in the ways the input controls check, so no endpoint control addresses it.

remediation_detail.limitation: This is a model-level weakness. No endpoint control fixes it, and inventing one would misrepresent the finding; the fix above is an evaluation and retraining procedure instead.

limitations: Drift is measured against each endpoint's own clean prediction, never the dataset label a baseline sentence was written to represent. Where a baseline does not predict its intended label the comparison remains valid, and no model-accuracy claim in this analysis rests on those baselines.

V2's defenses are application-layer only; no retraining was done. V2 is therefore not expected to reduce model-level sensitivity to typos or other meaning-preserving perturbations. A perturbation finding that persists on V2 is an honest non-improvement, not a gap in the hardening.
A failed health check records observed unavailability only. It is not evidence that the operating-system process died, and no process-death claim is made anywhere here.

Validity tiers are preserved per finding. Most of the suite is SILVER -- mechanically justified but not hand-verified -- so findings resting on SILVER evidence carry weaker semantic assurance than GOLD ones.

controls.note: Per-control counts overlap: a case may target more than one control. They are not a disjoint partition and must not be summed.

interpretation.classes_are_intent: Coverage classes record intended input-control coverage taken from case and control construction. They are not effectiveness and not causal attribution.
interpretation.cross_cutting_error_handling: The scoped exception handler is cross-cutting: its observable responses are reported, but no isolated causal proof is claimed for it.
interpretation.shared_framework_behaviour: Strict type/schema cases exercise a declared control even where both wrappers already reject the input at the framework layer; see incremental_vs_v1 rather than deleting the cases.
